precepts.text: Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same. Be ye not afraid neither doubt; for God is your guide, and the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves. So this is the same thing Noah was preaching back then, but nobody listened. Everybody mocked him.
precepts.point: For in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
Christ said “Watch therefore” and “Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.” Brothers and sisters, we have to be ready. Ezra gives the Lord's word to those who are: “Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same.”

The days of trouble are at hand, but the Lord will deliver his beloved from them. “Be ye not afraid neither doubt; for God is your guide, And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” God is the guide of those who keep his commandments and precepts; they are the ones left when the others are taken to destruction.

This is the same thing Noah was preaching back then, but nobody listened; everybody mocked him. The message is the same now: keep the commandments, don't let your sins weigh you down, and be ready, because the day comes in an hour you think not.

precepts.text: Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sins. You cannot openly seek his face while you are hiding your sins.
precepts.point: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory. When we behold the glass openly, we change. There is supposed to be a change in us.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Paul says we “have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. Why must they be renounced and not hidden? “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.”

God knows your inventions and the thoughts of your heart. He knows them that sin and would hide their sin. You cannot openly seek his face while you are hiding your sins, trying to get around them and not deal with them.

The open face of 2 Corinthians 3:18 is a face with nothing hidden. Beholding the glory of the Lord in his book means seeing what is there about ourselves and bringing it into the light: not walking in craftiness, not snaking around it, not handling the word of God deceitfully.

So the man who hides his sin is not beholding with an open face, and he is not changed into the same image from glory to glory. He only fools himself, because the Lord already knows what he thinks in his heart.

precepts.text: He is the guide of them who keep his commandments: let not your sins weigh you down. When you fall, Satan gets in your ear and whispers, you are no good, you need to leave this truth, God cannot use a person like you. Well, he used Samson, he used David, he used a lot of our forefathers that fell to sin. And let not your iniquities lift up themselves: do not let them rise back up in your body. But woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities, like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through. Just like no man can travel through that path, we cannot reach you with the scriptures any more; your heart is hardened, sin has dominated your life, and you are not you any more. It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed. Death and destruction is the final outcome. Stop.
precepts.point: And such were some of you: everybody in here can identify with something on that list and say, I used to do that. But ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God. We are washed with the word of God.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
What happens when sin reigns in your body and has dominion over you? “And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” He is the guide of those who keep his commandments and precepts.

“let not your sins weigh you down”: sometimes you fall in the midst of sin, and Satan gets in your ear and whispers, you're no good, you need to leave this truth, the Lord can't use a person like you. Well, he used Samson. He used David. He used a lot of our forefathers that fell to sin. “and let not your iniquities lift up themselves”: don't let them rise back up in your body again.

“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through!” You may say, I'm not bound with my sin. Bound in your sins is sin reigning in your body and having dominion over you. Just like no man can travel through that path, we can't reach you with the scriptures any more. Your heart is hardened, your sin has dominated your life, and you're not you anymore. The scriptures have no effect on you.

“It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Death and destruction: that is the final outcome, brothers. Stop watching the porn. “And such were some of you: but ye are washed”: that is the way out, not staying bound.

precepts.text: Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment; but for all these things they shall not turn from their wickedness. Vittles shall be so good cheap upon earth that they shall think themselves to be in good case, and even then shall evils grow upon earth: sword, famine, and great confusion. Many shall perish of famine, and the other that escape the hunger shall the sword destroy.
precepts.point: Discussion of Idi Amin, Uganda, and South Africa: Idi Amin expelled the Asian and European merchants from Uganda and handed their businesses to Ugandans who had no experience in the imports and exports of that merchandise, and the stores collapsed. Today in South Africa the xenophobia is the same error: legal migrants from Ghana, Nigeria, and the ECOWAS region with legitimate small businesses are being beaten, driven from hospitals, and flown home, while about 90 percent of the businesses and the land are owned by white people. They turn against their own brothers while the real owners of the country are standing in front of them. Black people in America do the same thing when we riot and burn down stores in our own neighborhoods instead of saving our money and opening our own. Nobody has solutions to the problems, and the white man's solution is jail time.
precepts.why:
Ezra explains why famines come: “Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment.” “But for all these things they shall not turn from their wickedness, nor be always mindful of the scourges.”

Scourges come, like what happened with George Floyd among us, and 9/11. But our people tend to forget. Civil rights came around 1964 and 1965, 62 years ago, and people said it could never happen again, the same way people in South Africa act like apartheid never happened. Now they are bringing back vagrancy laws under the 13th Amendment, where the homeless get arrested and prison labor becomes slavery again. They are redrawing district lines, as with the Texas map that moves Representative Jasmine Crockett's home out of her district, so black representatives lose their seats and our people lose their voice in Congress.

“Behold, victuals shall be so good cheap upon earth, that they shall think themselves to be in good case, and even then shall evils grow upon earth, sword, famine, and great confusion.” While food is cheap and everybody thinks things are fine, supermarkets are being moved out of our communities and our people are being priced off the cruise lines and airlines. The evils are growing behind the scenes.

And nobody has solutions. Idi Amin expelled the Asian and European merchants from Uganda and handed their businesses to Ugandans who had no experience in the imports and exports, and the stores collapsed. South Africa today beats and drives out legal migrants from Ghana, Nigeria and the ECOWAS region who own small stores, while about 90 percent of the businesses and the land belong to white people: they turn against their own brothers while the real owners of the country stand in front of them. Black people in America burn down stores in our own neighborhoods instead of saving our money and opening our own, and the white man's solution is jail time.

“For many of them that dwell upon earth shall perish of famine; and the other, that escape the hunger, shall the sword destroy.” The Bible is telling you famine is coming upon the earth, even though people say, never in America. Egypt had its famine in Joseph's day, and it will come again.

precepts.text: Lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily besets us and run the race with patience: you cannot win a race on a timer while carrying weights, and walking it is not winning at all.
precepts.point: Left undressed, like a lawn never mowed, the field is cast into the fire. Reject help and stay to yourself and destruction is the only thing left.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
The Lord says to them who keep his commandments and precepts, “let not your sins weigh you down.” Sin feels good. The pleasure comes, and once the pleasure is gone the guilt rolls in, and you feel like crap. After a while it becomes a burden, and it shows on you. Many of us came into the school guilty of things too shameful to confess, and some are still doing them. When you come forward and confess, you feel that weight lifted off: thank God.

Paul uses the same picture: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.” Lay aside every weight. Your sins of character are weights.

If you run a race carrying weights, can you run fast? No. You can still be in the race, but you either keep adding weight until you come in last and never cross the finish line, or you take the weights off. One weight off and you feel lighter; another off and you are faster. You were in third, now second, now first.

Some of y’all say, I’m good back here, I’ll just walk. Meanwhile you are on a timer, and time at the end is running out. A race is won by the time you run. If you are walking in a race, you are not winning at all, by no account.

That is why we lay aside every weight: the sins that so easily beset us are what hold us back. It is what 2 Esdras means: do not let your sins weigh you down.

precepts.text: Behold the word of the Lord, receive it: believe not the gods of whom the Lord spake.
precepts.point: Forcing the nations to unite under a new world government. So that's all I wanted.
precepts.why:
“Behold, the word of the Lord, receive it: believe not the gods of whom the Lord spake.” Receive it means believe it. Receive the word of the Lord, and do not believe these false gods out here.

It is the same warning Christ gave in Matthew 24: “Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not.” Whatever they show in the sky with their signs and wonders, the word of the Lord is what we receive, and the gods the Lord spoke against, the new gods that came newly up, we do not believe.

That is how the elect are kept from being deceived: not by what they see, but by holding to the word, because Christ said, “Behold, I have told you before.”

precepts.text: Send him to labour that he be not idle, for idleness teacheth much evil.
precepts.point: They that consent unto them shall be had in derision and trodden under foot: nobody likes a traitor, and like the donkeys in Planet of the Apes, Esau uses you and gets rid of you. In every place and in the next cities a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord, which is why Christ said flee to the next city.
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. That great multitude is what Christ said: you shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And “they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle”. Idle, i-d-l-e: a person avoiding work; lazy, indolent, slothful, workshy, shiftless, loafing; without purpose or effect, pointless.

In this truth, if you are idle you are avoiding work. Not work in the world: God's work. You are lazy in this truth. You have no purpose; you are just here. Some of you have been here for years and you have no office, doing nothing. You are idle.

“Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.” Brothers and sisters, when you are idle in the truth, you are learning evil. That is why you spend your time on porn, smoking cigarettes, smoking weed, hitting women up in their DMs. You have idle time, and there is a whole lot of work in this truth to be done.

We can spot that idleness as soon as you come in: the one who sits down and just looks around, looking at the women's side, taking no notes. If this means something to you, you are engulfed in it; you are writing things down and trying to put it to memory. The idle are the certain ones the multitude will take away and feed.

precepts.text: In the latter times some depart from the faith to doctrines of devils, forbidding to marry and commanding to abstain from meats which God created to be received with thanksgiving of them which know the truth, sanctified by the word in Leviticus 11.
precepts.point: They that consent unto them shall be had in derision and trodden under foot: nobody likes a traitor, and like the donkeys in Planet of the Apes, Esau uses you and gets rid of you. In every place and in the next cities a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord, which is why Christ said flee to the next city.
precepts.why:
The idle will be fed “with things offered unto idols.” Idols in the Bible are statues, figurines, golden calves, and also money, career and power that compete with God for worship. So what is the most idolatrous religion here in America? Christianity. You may think that is biased; Paul identifies the religion.

“Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”. This is the latter times. Why will some give heed to seducing spirits? Because you are idle; you have idle time. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: I believe in God, but I am not going to do anything the Bible says. “having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry”: what religion forbids men to marry? Catholics; that is Christianity. “and commanding to abstain from meats”: who cannot eat meat for 40 days? Catholics; they call it Lent.

Those meats “God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and the truth is God's law. “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Where is the food sanctified by the word of God? Leviticus 11.

The Roman Catholic Church is the mother church of every Protestant denomination on the tree: Orthodox, Jehovah's Witness, Presbyterian, Lutheran, Methodist, Episcopalian, Mormon, Evangelical, Pentecostal, Baptist, Adventist, Anglican, all the way to Christian nationalism. That is the idolatry the multitude will feed the idle, and they are already saying out loud that they are going to impose it on this country.

What do all those churches have in common? They worship the image of the beast. “And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” Their blasphemy is the perversion of the gospel of Christ, the perversion of the truth.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them”. Esau made war with us: Rome, Spain, Portugal. Pope Nicholas V made that edict to enslave us and force us into Christianity. And they overcame us; they enslaved us. “and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.”

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: the same man that overcame us. A book published in 1920, The Pillory, the Tale of the Borgia Pope, says it is an open secret that Cesare Borgia, son of Pope Alexander, posed for the image of Jesus. Salvatore, the savior: that is Cesare Borgia. Even Muslims will tell you that image is Jesus; ask a Buddhist and he will say the same. Everybody acknowledges it as Jesus the Christ.

All that worship him are those “whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” That is the idol the multitude will feed to the idle.

precepts.text: The dragon was wroth with the woman and went to make war, physical war, with the remnant of her seed which keep the commandments and have the testimony of Jesus: France already says shut down IUIC for teaching a black Jesus.
precepts.point: They that consent unto them shall be had in derision and trodden under foot: nobody likes a traitor, and like the donkeys in Planet of the Apes, Esau uses you and gets rid of you. precepts.why:
In every place and in the next cities there shall be “a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” Revelation shows who is behind it: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.”

The dragon is wroth: our enemies see us and they are angry. That is why in France they already said, shut down IUIC; a black Jesus, the Israelites, that is anti-semitic, we cannot allow this to go on. And he went to make war with the remnant: that is physical war, not only spiritual. That is tribulation, Jacob's trouble, persecution against those who keep the commandments and the testimony of Jesus Christ.

Christ warned of the same: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” You say you would never consent to their religion, but a whip across your back will change some of you, and you will be compelled to blaspheme.

And those who consent will be had in derision. Nobody likes a traitor. Like the apes in Planet of the Apes who betrayed their own and wore the word donkey before they were killed, Esau will use you and get rid of you. The ones who keep the commandments and the testimony are the ones the dragon makes war with; that is why Christ said, if they persecute you in this city, flee to the next.

precepts.text: Antiochus wrote that all should be one people and leave their laws, and many Israelites consented, sacrificed to idols, profaned the Sabbath and left their children uncircumcised, and whosoever would not obey should die: the same thing Spain and Portugal did to our people, and there is no new thing under the sun.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
“They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” We read the book of Acts and think that could never happen again, but Paul himself said, “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” The prophecy says it is going to happen again, and it happened under the Greeks too.

“Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king. Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” That is what is going to happen again. It happened in the time of Paul, in the time of the Maccabees, in Babylon when they tried to get us to worship the false god. That which has been is that which shall be; there is no new thing under the sun. Idolatry: leave that God and come worship this god.

They sent letters “that they should follow the strange laws of the land”, profane the sabbaths and festival days, sacrifice swine's flesh, leave their children uncircumcised, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances. And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.” You think they cannot make a Sunday law and say, that Sabbath thing, no, worship God on the day we say?

The same thing we read in the Maccabees is what Rome, Spain and Portugal did to our people in the Inquisition; read Jews and Moors. And you say it can never happen, this is the United States of America? It happened during slavery. The same thing.

precepts.why:
“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” They did it in the time of Rome, when the Pharisees did it with Rome's guidance. Paul tells the Hebrews, “For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.”

Ye had compassion of me in my bonds: when Paul was in prison, they supported him. And they took joyfully the spoiling, the robbing, of their goods: their homes and houses, lands and properties. Those Israelites sacrificed their whole livelihood. They knew that supporting Paul would reveal them, and whatever they had would be taken.

Are we prepared for that? Do we really think about it? The cushy side of the room: I'm so comfortable, I got my new house, my new car, my new hair, my new nails. Are you ready for what the scriptures say is going to happen? Are we willing to lose everything, knowing we have in heaven a better and enduring substance? That is another level of faith we have to build ourselves up to in the short, limited time we have.

Even the world is warning that if a crisis comes and the government says get on a bus for your safety, do not get on: prepare your food, water, power and shelter so you do not have to rely on them. We have been telling our people that for years.

“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.” That verse is very important, because it goes back to what Christ said: “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.”

Christ is talking about tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble. So what will the chosen be saying about Christ in that day, will they deny him or confess him? They are going to confess him.

Why does it say “Then shall they be known”? Because right now everybody says they believe in the Lord. Women say it; men say it. But when this starts to happen, you are going to see who is real and who is fake. On that day the ones who confess Christ before their tormentors are the ones known to be his chosen, tried as gold in the fire, and he will confess them before his Father.

precepts.text: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God and no torment touches them; in the sight of the unwise they seem to die, but they are in peace, their hope full of immortality, and God proved them as gold in the furnace and received them as a burnt offering.

The chosen are “tried as the gold in the fire”, and Wisdom gives more detail. “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Christ said we will be afflicted, so what does no torment mean? That is the lake of fire. That torment will not touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery, And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” Christ said, fear not them which kill the body; fear him who can kill body and soul. Man cannot touch your soul. They seem to die because the body died, but the real man, the real woman, is not dead. We keep falling for Esau's craftiness: it's all over, we're finished. It is not over. They are in peace; that is sleep, rest.

“For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. Jacob's trouble is just a little chastisement. “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us. Everybody says they believe; he will say, let that one get caught early and see what they do. He found them worthy because they confessed Christ before their tormentors.

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the saints is as a burnt offering to the Lord. Christ gave his life, and he said if you will not take up your cross and follow him, you are not worthy of him.

Wisdom says the righteous are tried as gold in the furnace and received as a burnt offering. Christ said, “And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.”

Christians say that means you cannot pay your bills and you have to carry all your problems on your back. No, that is not what it is talking about. When Christ was carrying the cross, where did it lead him? To death. He is saying the same thing for us.

We have to be willing to sacrifice ourselves. That is what Wisdom of Solomon was just saying: the souls of the righteous who die for the truth are in the hand of God. If you cannot confess the Lord, even unto death, you are not worthy to be his disciple. That is the cross, and that is how the chosen will be known.

precepts.text: Herod killed James and jailed Peter; the church prayed in a safe house, and when the angel freed Peter they told the damsel she was mad and that it was his angel, because they thought he was dead and could not visit him. Peter was a fugitive for the rest of his life.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
“Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same. Be ye not afraid neither doubt”. Why neither doubt? Because doubt comes. My mama just got put to death, my children, my wife; Lord, are you going to save us? Remember John the Baptist when he was imprisoned; that little bit of doubt crept in. Acts shows the situation.

“Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)” James was beheaded; Peter was in prison. The angel brought Peter out, and he went to “the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.” That was a safe house where Israelites were hiding and praying. When the damsel knew Peter's voice, “they said unto her, Thou art mad”, and “Then said they, It is his angel.”

What did they think had happened to Peter? That he had been put to death. It shows you could not go visit him. There was no visitation, as there are prisons like Guantanamo Bay in Cuba today, with no lawyers and no visitors, and they are building more like it. So do not think, the brothers don't care about me, the sisters didn't come visit me. There will be places nobody can visit you. It is not that we do not care; we cannot get to you. All the saints could do was pray.

And Peter was on the run, a fugitive from the government the rest of his life. The Lord intervened for one and gave him more time, and the other, James, was killed. It is going to get like that, brothers and sisters. That is why we study, pray and apply: knowing ahead of time is supposed to strengthen your resolve, so that you are not afraid, neither doubt.

precepts.text: If we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves; if we confess our sins he is faithful and just to forgive: verse 9 is the difference between us and the Christian on the street.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
“for God is your guide, And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down”. Why say, let not your sins weigh you down? Because we do sin, and churches love to try to trap you with it. “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.”

Christians on the street will say, do you sin, my brother? Yes. But my sin cannot justify you continuing in sin. Verse 9 is the key; verse 9 is the difference between me and you.

When we start cutting them up, they say, you think you're better than us? Do you sin? Tell them yes, and go right here and show them the difference. They are liars, because they teach that you can sin with no consequences. We teach that if we do sin, the black Messiah laid down his life, if we believe on him, so that we can fight to stop sinning. Simple answer; don't let them jam you up.

We do make errors and fall into folly at times. Confess it and keep fighting, and let not your sins weigh you down.

precepts.text: Abstain from fleshly lusts which war against the soul: pornography is not normal, it means fornication, and it is a war for your soul, from the magazines in the ceiling to easy access today.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
“let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”. When you keep entertaining that sin, eventually you will be bound by it. Peter says, “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”.

This is a spiritual war, a war for your soul. Take porn. Brothers say, I got it under control; it don't bother me. No, you don't have it under control. Picture a hallway of doors. A lot of you say, I only watch straight porn, like it is a good thing. That is door number one. Then the threesome, then the train. After a while you get desensitized; that does not excite you anymore, so you go to the next door down: chicks with dicks, then bestiality, then scat, then lesbian, then pedophilia. That is where the doors lead.

It is not normal. And you know it is the devil: when the Bishop was a little kid, his father had magazines hidden up in the drop ceiling. How did two little boys know to get a chair and climb up there, when they never saw their father do it? Playboy, Hustler, then VHS, then DVDs, and today easy access in your hand.

That is how iniquity lifts itself up until you are bound with your sins, covered like a field with thorns. Abstain from fleshly lusts; they are at war with your soul.

precepts.text: Sin shall not have dominion over you, for ye are not under the law of sacrifice but under grace; shall we sin then? God forbid. His servants ye are to whom ye obey, and if you wake, work and sleep thinking of porn, that is your god.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
When you keep entertaining a sin, it binds you. Paul says, “For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.” We are not under the law of sacrifice, but under grace. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.”

“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” His servants ye are to whom ye obey. If you wake up thinking about porn, go to work thinking about porn, and go to sleep thinking about porn, that is your god. You are its servant.

Grace is not a license to keep sinning; it is so that sin shall not have dominion over you. Christ laid down his life so we could fight to stop sinning, not so we could be bound in it. And when you are bound, there is no magic scripture that will release you; you have to want to be released.

precepts.text: It is impossible to renew again to repentance those once enlightened who fall away back into their sin or false religion; that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected and its end is to be burned, the same as 2 Esdras 16:78.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through! It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Hebrews says the same thing.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance”. Those who were once enlightened, who came into this truth, and fall away back into their sin or back into false religion: it is impossible to renew them again to repentance.

“For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.”

That is the field of 2 Esdras 16:78, covered with thorns, left undressed and cast into the fire. The ground that drinks in the word and brings forth fruit receives blessing; the one bound with its sins and bearing thorns ends in the fire.

precepts.text: As a woman in the ninth month brings forth within two or three hours with pains that slack not, so shall the plagues not be slack to come upon the earth. In the time of nations, hours are years and months.
precepts.point: Contractions come and ease and come again closer together. A pain comes one month, things calm, another comes two or three months later. When it calms, Israelites say nothing is going to happen and go back to business as usual. The real brothers and sisters do not need warning.
precepts.why:
Paul says, “For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.” Peace and safety is what Trump keeps saying, the peace president who bombed Yemen, Somalia, Iraq, Iran, Syria, Nigeria and Venezuela. Some of you love it when the president talks about peace, stomping your feet because you think nothing is going to happen in this country. Ezra shows what travail upon a woman with child means.

“As when a woman with child in the ninth month bringeth forth her son, with two or three hours of her birth great pains compass her womb, which pains, when the child cometh forth, they slack not a moment.” Within two or three hours: in the time of nations that is two or three years, or months. When a woman is having a baby, her contractions come ten minutes apart, then five, six, five, four, closer and closer.

“Even so shall not the plagues be slack to come upon the earth, and the world shall mourn, and sorrows shall come upon it on every side.” A pain comes one month, then things calm down; another comes two or three months later, and things calm down again. That is how it is going to be in this world.

But when things calm down, Israelites say nothing is going to happen and go back to business as usual. That is why Paul says “of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.” We read the prophecies every week, and if you are not paying attention you will be caught off guard. The real brothers and the real sisters will not need to be warned; they are aware of what is about to happen.

precepts.text: In the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, speaking lies in hypocrisy, forbidding to marry and commanding to abstain from meats. Forbidding to marry is Catholicism; abstaining from meat is Lent. That is the food offered to idols.
precepts.point: Digital currency is how they will control it. China deletes money from your account for jaywalking; imagine the order that you may not teach the gospel or gather on the seventh day, and your account is hit when you do.
precepts.why:
The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” What does that mean? It is talking about Christianity. If you are idle, they are going to feed you Christianity. How do we know? Paul prophesied it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”.

We already know some of you are going to depart from this faith. Why? Because persecution is coming, and when you cannot pay your bills and cannot get food, you will leave. America wants to bring in digital currency so they can control us. In China, if you jaywalk, they take money out of your account; imagine being told you may not teach the gospel or gather on the seventh day, and when we do it anyway, your digital bank account is hit.

What is the doctrine of devils? Paul explains it: “Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats”. What religion forbids men to marry? Catholicism, Christianity. Commanding to abstain from meats: that is Lent, no meat for 40 days. That is the food offered to idols: Christianity, Roman Catholicism.

Why will they feed it to you? Because you do not study. When persecution comes, you are fearful, you cannot endure to the end, so you give up and betray the King of kings. And “they that consent unto them shall be had in derision and in reproach, and trodden under foot.” Even the white man hates a traitor. In the Planet of the Apes the apes who betrayed their own wore the word donkey on their backs, and when they were no longer needed, they were killed. Then you face the King, and the lake of fire. But those who endure, “Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

precepts.text: So shall righteousness hate iniquity when she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face; the Lord defends him that diligently searcheth out every sin. Discipline your mind to hate iniquity. Wisdom of Solomon 5:13-15: the hope of the ungodly is dust blown away and the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day, but the righteous live for evermore and their reward is with the Lord. Do the homework and you live forever while the instant feelings pass.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.
precepts.why:
“So shall righteousness hate iniquity, when she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face, when he cometh that shall defend him that diligently searcheth out every sin upon earth.” We have to learn to hate iniquity. We have to discipline our minds to hate iniquity and to hate sin. If we want the Lord to defend us, that is what we have to do.

Wisdom of Solomon shows the end of both sides. The ungodly say, “Even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to shew; but were consumed in our own wickedness.” The hope of the ungodly “is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.”

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” You may not see it right now, but if you keep God’s commandments, if you do the homework, you are going to live forever, while everything that feels good in the moment passes away. The Most High cares for you, if you are able to hate sin.

That is the answer to the hasty man: discipline the mind to hate iniquity, and the Lord defends the one who diligently searches out every sin.

precepts.text: Surely he knoweth your inventions and what you think in your heart, even them that sin and would hide their sin. We sin and hide it; the Lord knows why you watch what you watch at night and why you smell like weed at the door.
precepts.point: The burden of Babylon which Isaiah saw: lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, the government, America; the banner is the Bible. Exalt the voice unto them, as Isaiah 58:1 says lift it up like a trumpet and spare not, and shake the hand, warn our people, that they may go into the gates of the nobles. In the midst of the war Isaiah sees the prophets still going out.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
We are to persuade our people, but this is what we have to overcome: “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.” That is what we do. We sin, and we hide our sin.

The Lord says, I know your inventions. I know why you watch HBO at night; I know why you like Spartacus, why you like Power. I know you love to smoke weed and spray yourself with cologne right before you come to the Sabbath, and then security says, that brother smells like weed. Keep smoking weed and you will end up face down in the street like the man in the video, calling the officer papi.

Some brothers are tied to unbelieving wives who cook pork on the same grill next to your lawful food, still go to the club and don't respect you, and you refuse to leave. Sisters are tied to unbelieving men. There is no love among our people, and we are caught up in these sins, lawless, like 1 Timothy 1:9.

You can hide it from the brothers and the sisters, but you cannot hide it from the Lord. He knows your inventions and what you think in your heart. So before we can persuade our people, we have to get ourselves right.

precepts.text: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?
precepts.point: Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you live, you still have it.
precepts.why:
The Lord God says, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” And: “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes.” Brothers give up their position because of the affliction, the little tribulation, or because of their bills, two hundred-some thousand dollars of debt. How could you be that stupid, that ignorant? We all have bills. That is all you have. Their sin is wearing them down so much, and they are so covered with it that they cannot see the brotherhood right in front of them.

David asks the question every one of us has to answer: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” You have to stand up.

The evildoers are where we are today. Taking a man out of his country and bringing him back to America: the same America that pushes democracy, when democracy put him there, kidnaps him and charges him with unjust judgment. Is that just, or wicked? If it is hard for you to see that America is evil, it is because you are evil yourself. Everything here is a work of iniquity; they push sin everywhere, even in a little karate flick.

Christ said, “I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world.” Have the word of God and the world will hate you, and your family will hate you. “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.” He left us in the world because we have a path to go through: from Adam until now it has been good against evil, and our job is to stand for what is right. “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The stony ground “immediately receive it with gladness”, but has no root, and when affliction arises “immediately they are offended.” What have you given for this truth? Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are the children of Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you are alive, you still have it. So who will rise up and stand? Do not let your sins weigh you down.

precepts.text: They shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour.
precepts.point: The idle in the truth will be fed Christianity. Those two years or more in the congregation must examine themselves.
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. Who is this great multitude that is over us? It is law enforcement, their military, set over the believing Israelites. Isaiah proves it.

“In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof”. This Egypt is a spiritual Egypt: America. An altar is used for sacrifice, so there is going to be a lot of death. “And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors”.

Why would we cry unto the Lord? Because of the oppressors, with an s on it: more than one. That is the great multitude whose burning wrath is kindled over us. That is Jacob's trouble, and we have not gotten to that part yet.

So the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16 is the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the power of spiritual Egypt that will be over our people in this land, and it is because of them that Israel will cry unto the Lord.

precepts.text: Spare thy people, O Lord, wherefore should they say, Where is their God?
precepts.point: The idle in the truth will be fed Christianity. Those two years or more in the congregation must examine themselves.
precepts.why:
Joel shows the same cry. “Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly”, and “Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

Why will we cry, Spare thy people? We just read it in Isaiah 19: because of the oppressors. They will say, we killed you, where is your God? We cut your throat, we ended your bank account, where is your God?

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He pities his people because we are not in the land. But he promises not to leave us alone: “Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil”, “and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen”.

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army”. That is the name the Bible gives to the power that is going to be on us: the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16, is the northern army. He will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, the Dead Sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, the Mediterranean, “and his stink shall come up”. The white man shall meet death when he goes to that land, because he has done evil things.

precepts.text: Idleness teacheth much evil.
precepts.point: The idle in the truth will be fed Christianity. Those two years or more in the congregation must examine themselves.
precepts.why:
The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” Spell that word: i-d-l-e. “Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.”

Idle means a person avoiding work: lazy, indolent, slothful, shiftless, inactive, sluggish, lethargic; without purpose or effect. Those words fit some of you in here, men and women. Not the new people who just came, but those who have been with us two years or more. What are you doing? Do you have an office? Is there something you are doing here in Israel? If not, you are idle, and idleness teaches much evil.

And what will the idle be fed? Things offered unto idols, i-d-o-l: an image or representation of a god used as an object of worship. Look at the images of the Roman Catholic Church; those are idols. One word: Christianity.

So the ones the multitude takes away and feeds with idolatry are the ones with no purpose in here. Because you were idle, you will be seduced and given Christianity, that idolatrous religion. Stay busy in the work of the Most High.

precepts.text: The Lord that made heaven and earth by the word knoweth all the works of men and their hearts.
precepts.point: That is the judgment on the willful: if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins. That man knew the law; it was not ignorance, it was blatant. The Lord knoweth all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts; he knoweth your inventions and what ye think in your heart, even them that sin and would hide their sin. Sin willfully and your grace period is up.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
“Behold, the Lord knoweth all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts: Which spake but the word, Let the earth be made; and it was made: Let the heaven be made; and it was created.”

The same Lord that made heaven and earth by the word knows all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts. So He knows whether a ruler did somewhat through ignorance or willfully; nothing about the sin is hid from Him.

precepts.text: He knoweth your inventions, even them that sin and would hide their sin; nothing willful is hid from him.
precepts.point: That is the judgment on the willful: if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins. That man knew the law; it was not ignorance, it was blatant. The Lord knoweth all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts; he knoweth your inventions and what ye think in your heart, even them that sin and would hide their sin. Sin willfully and your grace period is up.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
“Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.”

Nothing willful is hid from Him. The one who sins and then says he knew it not, hiding his sin under ignorance, is known for what he is. He that pondereth the heart considers it, and that is why the law separates the sin of ignorance, which has its atonement, from the presumptuous sin, which is cut off.

precepts.text: Woe unto Babylon, Asia, Egypt, and Syria; destruction is coming on them all.
precepts.point: The Lord will be terrible unto them and famish all the gods of the earth, and men shall worship Him every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen. That is why Balaam said he shall behold Him, but not nigh: the nations will worship from their own place and come up only at the appointed times of the year.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The Sceptre out of Israel smites the corners of Moab and destroys all the children of Sheth: Moab the Chinese, Ammon the Japanese, and Sheth going into the Egyptian. Esdras names them together: “Woe be unto thee, Babylon, and Asia! woe be unto thee, Egypt and Syria!”

Woe unto Babylon, Asia, Egypt, and Syria; destruction is coming on them all in the latter days Balaam saw.

precepts.text: The Lord sends his sword, fire, and plagues, and none can turn them back.
precepts.point: Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth and their seed from among the children of men; Esau is not going to be no more. They imagined a mischievous device which they are not able to perform; the Most High makes their devices of none effect and makes ready his arrows against the face of them.

note.label: Psalm 21: Victory Through the King and the Enemy Destroyed

precepts.why:
“Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.” Esau is not going to be no more. Ezra shows there is no stopping it: “A sword is sent upon you, and who may turn it back? A fire is sent among you, and who may quench it? Plagues are sent unto you, and what is he that may drive them away?”

“May any man drive away an hungry lion in the wood? or may any one quench the fire in stubble, when it hath begun to burn?” The Lord sends his sword, fire, and plagues, and none can turn them back. They imagined a mischievous device they are not able to perform, but the Most High's arrows are made ready against the face of them, and nobody drives them away.

precepts.text: In the days of trouble the Most High delivers his beloved and guides them that keep his commandments.
precepts.point: The Most High led the teaching straight to that scripture; the Bible precepts link together because he leads his people to the places they need.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
Through Ezra the Most High speaks to his beloved: “Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same.” The days of trouble are coming, but he delivers his own out of them. “Be ye not afraid neither doubt; for God is your guide”. That is the same promise David closes Psalm 48 with: “he will be our guide even unto death.” This God is our God for ever and ever, and he guides Israel through the trouble, so there is no cause to be afraid or to doubt.

He is “the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts”. The guiding is for the ones keeping his commandments; that is who walks about Zion, marks her bulwarks and tells it to the generation following. And he adds, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.”

The Most High led the teaching straight to this scripture. The Bible precepts link together like that, because he leads his people to the places they need.

precepts.text: This says the same thing as Psalm 119, that the Most High guides them who keep His commandments and precepts, and that we must not let our sins weigh us down.
